lines: {"concept_id": "drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry", "kind": "formula", "contract": "Road user x has entered structure region r and has not since stood clear of it by clearance: x entered r (drv.motion.entering_region: its footprint overlaps r at that observation and did not at the observation before) at the observation or at an earlier one, and at every observation from that entry up to the observation the ground distance from x's body outline to r (st.region_geometry, m, world frame; zero while the footprint overlaps r) has stayed below clearance. It becomes true at an entry, holds while x stays on r or within clearance of it, becomes false at the first observation at which x's body stands at clearance or more from r, and stays false until x's next entry. Unknown where it is undecided whether x entered r at an observation since which the distance stayed below clearance (at x's first observation, whether it entered there is unknown), or where the distance is unobserved at an observation that decides it. Not denoted: the side of r on which the body stands (a body that backs out of r and stays within clearance of it still holds), x's direction or speed, or a halt: the caller reads those.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "x", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [{"name": "clearance", "unit": "m", "meaning": "the ground distance from x's body outline to r at or beyond which x counts as clear of r; the caller passes the distance its words state"}], "elements": [{"span": "x entered r (drv.motion.entering_region: its footprint overlaps r at that observation and did not at the observation before)", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": ["drv.motion.entering_region"], "justification": "The entry is the co-proposed concept drv.motion.entering_region, whose contract is “Road user x enters structure region r at the observation: its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before”; it is the event from which the state is counted, and the formula's past operator (since) reads it at the observation it occurred. rel.occupies is the atom the entry reads: “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”."}, {"span": "the ground distance from x's body outline to r (st.region_geometry, m, world frame; zero while the footprint overlaps r)", "atoms": ["st.region_geometry"], "concepts": [], "justification": "st.region_geometry carries “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)”. Not a stand-in for occupancy: the state does not read the distance as occupancy; the entry is read through rel.occupies, and the distance only decides when the body stands clear."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "x does not overlap r at its first observations and stands farther than clearance from it; its footprint overlaps r from the third observation; at the sixth it has left r and its body outline stands at a distance below clearance from r. {"concept_id": "drv.motion.stopping_distance", "kind": "quantity", "contract": "The distance road user x would cover from the observation to a standstill if it kept its present speed for reaction_time and then slowed at the constant deceleration deceleration: its speed (kin.speed, m/s) times reaction_time, plus the square of its speed divided by twice deceleration; in metres, zero for a body at a standstill. Not denoted: the distance x actually covers before a later halt, the deceleration the surface, the grade or the vehicle allows (the caller passes deceleration), whether anything lies within the distance, or whether x is required to stop.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "x", "sort": "track"}], "params": [{"name": "reaction_time", "unit": "s", "meaning": "the time over which x keeps its speed before braking begins"}, {"name": "deceleration", "unit": "m/s^2", "meaning": "the constant deceleration at which x slows once braking begins; strictly positive"}], "elements": [{"span": "its speed (kin.speed, m/s)", "atoms": ["kin.speed"], "concepts": [], "justification": "kin.speed is the “magnitude of velocity” in m/s, the one measured input of the distance. Not a stand-in for acceleration: the deceleration is the caller's parameter, never read from kin.accel_longitudinal."}], "residues": [], "literals": [{"value": 2, "unit": "ratio", "why": "the factor of uniformly decelerated motion: a body slowing at constant deceleration from a speed covers the square of the speed divided by twice the deceleration"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "x moves at a steady speed; the instance fixes reaction_time and deceleration, and its bounds bracket the speed times reaction_time plus the squared speed over twice deceleration: the value lies in the bounds."}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "x moves at a higher steady speed with the same instance parameters and the same bounds: the computed distance lies above the upper bound."}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "As holds, but the source does not observe x's speed at the observation.", "masked": ["kin.speed"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_600_1a", "NRS_484D_215_1_o1"], "supersedes": null}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_560_7a", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-560-7a"], "subject": {"binder": "x", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.", "role": "definitional"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so it is claimed as one atom, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”; the reading classifies the classes under it by the definition's words “every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; ... (4) An electric scooter”, so its exclusions are the reading's and are not expanded here. Its exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “driver” (DEF-NRS-484A-080, “every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle”) is not read as membership but through the vehicle's controlled motion (the agency reading on s1)."}, {"span": "s2", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.railway_crossing", "st.region_geometry"], "derived": ["drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry", "drv.motion.entering_region"], "justification": "“crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad” is a level crossing: st.railway_crossing is the “level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail”; “railroad” (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is “a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails”, and the atom's word “railway” already leaves out a streetcar line laid in the street, which is not a railway level crossing, so no further condition is needed. The subject is crossing from its entry onto the crossing (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies: “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”) until it has completely crossed it, which is drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with the clearance s4 states: the concept reads st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”. The crossing r is the subject's own: anchored by rel.occupies at the entry and by the distance since, never any crossing of the scene."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": ["kin.speed", "dev.human_direction", "dev.governs", "rel.occupies", "st.travel_region"], "derived": ["drv.motion.halted"], "justification": "“to fail to completely cross ... without stopping”: “stopping” is DEF-NRS-484A-260, “any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_560_7a", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-560-7a"], "subject": {"binder": "x", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.", "role": "definitional"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so it is claimed as one atom, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”; the reading classifies the classes under it by the definition's words “every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; ... (4) An electric scooter”, so its exclusions are the reading's and are not expanded here. Its exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “driver” (DEF-NRS-484A-080, “every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle”) is not read as membership but through the vehicle's controlled motion (the agency reading on s1)."}, {"span": "s2", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.railway_crossing", "st.region_geometry"], "derived": ["drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry", "drv.motion.entering_region"], "justification": "“crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad” is a level crossing: st.railway_crossing is the “level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail”; “railroad” (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is “a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails”, and the atom's word “railway” already leaves out a streetcar line laid in the street, which is not a railway level crossing, so no further condition is needed. The subject is crossing from its entry onto the crossing (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies: “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”) until it has completely crossed it, which is drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with the clearance s4 states: the concept reads st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”. The crossing r is the subject's own: anchored by rel.occupies at the entry and by the distance since, never any crossing of the scene."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": ["kin.speed", "dev.human_direction", "dev.governs", "rel.occupies", "st.travel_region"], "derived": ["drv.motion.halted"], "justification": "“to fail to completely cross ... without stopping”: “stopping” is DEF-NRS-484A-260, “any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”. The halting is drv.motion.halted, “A road user is at a standstill at the observation ... the road user's speed (kin.speed, m/s) is at or below speed_floor ... with no minimum duration”, which keeps “even momentarily”; its own definition id (DEF-NRS-484A-255) is a required stop, but its contract denotes a standstill at an observation whatever the duty, which is what this halting is. A halt while the vehicle is crossing and has not completely crossed is the failure. The definition's exception for a direction of a police officer is carried beside it: dev.human_direction is “a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, ...}”, tied to the subject by dev.governs (“the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”) on a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and it is not read as one: it says which road users the direction is given to. The other parts of the definition's exception are read as the narrowings on s3 say."}, {"span": "s4", "atoms": ["st.region_geometry", "st.railway_crossing", "rel.occupies"], "derived": ["drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry"], "justification": "The section's own definition of “completely cross”: “the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail”. Once the body has left the crossing, the point of its outline nearest the crossing is its trailing end, so “trailing end ... 15 feet or more past” is the ground distance from the body outline to the crossing region (st.region_geometry: “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)”) at or above the literal 15 ft; drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry with clearance 15 ft is true from the entry until that first holds. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing “and its nearest rail”; rel.occupies anchors the entry."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "x", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and there is a railway level crossing r (st.railway_crossing) that x is crossing and has not completely crossed: drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with clearance the literal 15 ft of s4 — x's footprint entered r (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies) at the observation or earlier, and at every observation since its body outline has stood less than 15 ft from r (st.region_geometry distance; zero while on r). Read at every observation.", "obligation": "At every observation at which the applicability holds, x is not halted: drv.motion.halted(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution is false (a single observation at a standstill is a halt, since stopping is “any halting, even momentarily”). A halt does not violate where it is in compliance with a police officer's direction: some human direction d (dev.human_direction) with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region l (st.travel_region) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) at that observation. The obligation reads x's motion and the direction governing the region x is on; it needs no crossing of its own.", "params": ["p.speed_resolution"], "narrowings": [{"span": "s1", "why": "“the driver of any vehicle” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle crossing is taken to be driven, and the duty binds its conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}, {"span": "s3", "why": "“due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle” states why the vehicle stops; neither the room it would need beyond the crossing nor its undercarriage clearance over the crossing's profile is observable, so the cause is read through the conduct it explains: a halt while the vehicle is crossing and has not yet completely crossed. A halt on the crossing for another cause (a breakdown) is not told apart.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "purpose"}, {"span": "s3", "why": "The posted definition of stopping excepts a halt “necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic”. This section makes a halt due to insufficient space for the vehicle on the opposite side — the space that queued traffic or an object fills — the failure it forbids; reading that exception into it would empty clause (1). The rule therefore does not excuse a halt on the crossing because a road user stands ahead of the vehicle. Of the exception for “the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”, the police officer's direction to stop is read; no official device directs a halt on the crossing itself (the railway signal or gate directs a halt before it, which a vehicle already crossing has passed, and a signal or stop sign beyond directs a halt at its own line, queueing for which on the tracks is clause (1)), so no device direction is read.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "s3", "why": "“the nearest rail” is read as the boundary of the crossing region the map carries (st.railway_crossing with its nearest rail): the distance is measured from the body outline to that region, which is at the rail or beyond it.", "kind": "reading"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A passenger car (a class the reading includes under DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) drives along a roadway, enters a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing with its outline) and, with a truck queued just beyond the crossing, halts with its footprint still overlapping r for several observations. No human direction is in the scene."}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The car enters the crossing, travels across it at a steady speed without halting, and halts only well after its body outline has stood more than 15 ft past the crossing region."}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The car drives on a roadway with no railway crossing in the scene and halts at a stop line."}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "As forbid, but the source does not observe speed, so whether the car is halted on the crossing is unknown.", "masked": ["kin.speed"]}, {"name": "branch_1", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The car crosses the rails, leaves the crossing region, and halts behind a queue with its trailing end a short distance past the crossing, less than 15 ft from it."}, {"name": "branch_2", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The car halts on the crossing while a police officer (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop) governing the roadway the car occupies directs it to stop."}, {"name": "branch_3", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "No other road user is in the scene: the car crosses alone, its body outline reaches more than 15 ft past the crossing, and it halts there."}], "literals": [{"span": "s4", "text": "15 feet", "value": 15, "unit": "ft"}], "param_proposals": [{"name": "p.speed_resolution", "unit": "m/s", "value": 0.2, "convention": "Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.", "source": "speed noise of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard"}], "gaps": []}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_600_1a", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-600-1a"], "subject": {"binder": "x", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "at: A rate of speed", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.", "role": "standard"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "kin.speed"], "derived": ["drv.motion.moving"], "justification": "“a vehicle of any kind or character”: “vehicle” is DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and claimed as the one atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (“membership of a legal aggregate”); “of any kind or character” adds no class beyond the definition's. Each factor's magnitude enters its bound with the speed, so the bound moves with the factor's degree.", "surrogate": true}], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "x", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and is moving: drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution. Let S be x's stopping distance drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), the deceleration a selected by the surface with Term.cond: p.braking_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds; else p.braking_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds; else p.braking_decel_dry. (1) S is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance). (2) S is at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (3) v times v times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most p.curve_lateral_accel. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): p.lateral_margin_time times v is at most the lane's width (st.lane_width) less x's width (kin.extent, width). (5) For every road user y that is not x (same), is a member of the traffic aggregate (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) and is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): p.traffic_time_headway times v is at most the surface gap from x to y (rel.surface_gap).", "params": ["p.speed_resolution", "p.perception_reaction_time", "p.braking_decel_dry", "p.braking_decel_wet", "p.braking_decel_ice", "p.curve_lateral_accel", "p.lateral_margin_time", "p.traffic_time_headway"], "narrowings": [{"span": "s1", "why": "“any person to drive or operate” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven or operated, and the duty binds its speed whoever or whatever is at the controls.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}, {"span": "s3", "why": "The traffic is read through the members of the traffic aggregate ahead of the subject in its own lane, by the time gap to them at the subject's speed; {"node_id": "NRS_484B_769", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-769"], "subject": {"binder": "x", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle", "ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle", "ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "An operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "upon a roadway", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "shall give all signals by hand and arm", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "in the manner required by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420],", "role": "reference"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.", "role": "exception"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle", "ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle", "ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter"], "derived": [], "justification": "The three terms are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle (“a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride”), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle (“a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts”) and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter (“a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor”), each claimed as one ru.aggregate atom (“membership of a legal aggregate”), the same mapping the index records for “The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter”. # Plan — batch 04 (iteration 001)

Six nodes over five laws. Two new concept records: `drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry` and
`drv.motion.stopping_distance`. Reused concepts from earlier batches: `drv.motion.moving`,
`drv.motion.halted` and `drv.motion.entering_region`. No law-local aggregates. One atom gap, on
NRS-484D-100-1(c).

## NRS_484B_560_7a — complete the railroad crossing without stopping

**Decision.** The subject is a vehicle (`ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle`). The duty applies
while the vehicle is crossing a railway level crossing and has not completely crossed it. That state
is the new concept `drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r; clearance)`: it is true from the
vehicle's entry onto `st.railway_crossing` until its body outline stands at the clearance or more
from the crossing region (`st.region_geometry`). The clearance is the section's own literal, 15 ft.
Once the body has left the crossing, the trailing end is the point of the outline nearest the
crossing, so this distance measures the section's definition of "completely cross". While the duty
applies, the vehicle must not halt (`drv.motion.halted`, with no minimum duration, as in "any
halting, even momentarily").

**Reasons.**
- The causes "due to insufficient (1) space … or (2) undercarriage clearance" say why the vehicle
  stops. Neither cause is observable. Following the ontology's convention on purpose, they are read
  through the conduct they explain: a halt before the crossing is complete. This is disclosed as an
  `observable_reading` of category `purpose`.
- The definition of stopping excepts a halt "necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic". That
  exception is deliberately not read. Clause (1) makes a halt forced by queued traffic beyond the
  crossing the very violation, so reading the exception in would empty clause (1).
- The other part of the exception, a halt directed by a police officer, is carried
  (`dev.human_direction`, role `police_officer`, indication `stop`, governing the region the vehicle
  occupies).
- Directions from a device are not read. No official device directs a halt on the tracks: a signal
  or stop sign further on directs a halt at its own line, and queueing on the tracks for it is
  clause (1).
- "Nearest rail" is read as the boundary of the crossing region.

**Reversal signals:**
- A label that excuses a halt on the tracks behind a queue.
- An ontology atom for undercarriage clearance or for the crossing's vertical profile; that would
  let clause (2) be read on its own evidence.

## NRS_484B_600_1a — basic speed rule (surrogate)

**Decision.** The duty is a standard, so the node is marked surrogate. The subject is a moving
vehicle (`drv.motion.moving`). Each factor the words name has its own bound, and the speed enters
every bound:
- **Surface and weather.** The stopping distance (new quantity concept
  `drv.motion.stopping_distance`) uses a braking deceleration chosen by the surface: ice or snow,
  else wet or precipitation, else dry.
- **Other highway conditions.** The stopping distance must not exceed the sight distance
  (`st.sight_distance`). The speed squared times the road's curvature must not exceed a lateral
  acceleration.
- **Weather.** The stopping distance must not exceed the visibility distance (`env.visibility`).
- **Width.** A lateral margin proportional to speed must fit between the lane's width and the
  vehicle's width.
- **Traffic.** A time headway to every road user ahead in the same lane.

**Reasons.**
- The traffic aggregate is not claimed. The validator does not accept an aggregate inside an
  operationalization. A road user in the lane ahead is, by the definition's words, traffic "using
  any highway for purposes of travel", so the rule reads every such road user whatever its class.
- Each narrower reading (highway width read as lane width; the catch-all read only through sight
  distance and curvature) is disclosed on the standard span.

**Reversal signals:**
- Labelled verdicts that disagree systematically with one bound: tune that bound's parameter, or
  drop the bound.
- The operator rejecting the lateral-margin convention for width.

## NRS_484B_769 — cyclist and scooter signals by hand and arm

**Decision.** The subject belongs to one of three aggregates: bicycle, electric bicycle or electric
scooter. The rule applies on a roadway whenever the rider shows a signal, either a lit turn
indicator or an arm signal. The signal must then be given by arm (`sig.hand_signal` other than
`no_signal`), and its meaning must match any lit indicator. A left indicator matches either `left`
or `re_enter`, because NRS 484B.420 uses the same horizontal arm for both.

"In the manner required by NRS 484B.420" is a `definition` reference to DEF-NRS-484B-420. Its four
listed meanings are exactly the values of `sig.hand_signal`. The right-arm alternative in the
exception decodes to the meaning `right`, so it is accepted.

**Reason.** `sig.hand_signal` records only the meaning of a signal, not which arm or side gave it.
This is disclosed as a narrowing.

**Reversal signal:** an atom for arm posture (which arm, which side). With it, the manner could be
checked directly.

## NRS_484D_100_1 — when lighted lamps are required

**Decision.** The subject is a vehicle on a highway that is not parked. The rule applies at any one
of three times:
- (a) `env.darkness`, with its sunset/sunrise boundary set to the literal one-half hour;
- (b) `env.visibility` below the literal 1,000 ft, an `observable_reading` of category
  `perception`;
- (c) a sign directing lamps on, which is an atom gap.

The list is joined by "and", but it names the times at which the duty arises, so any one of them
suffices. The obligation is headlamps lit (low or high beam).

**Reasons.**
- The parked-vehicle exceptions point to the chapters' provisions on parking lamps. They are read as
  excusing a parked vehicle (at a standstill with its engine off) from this headlamp duty.
- The class-by-class lamp sets "as respectively required in this chapter" are not in the corpus.
  They are a residue on the reference span, and the headlamp reading is a disclosed narrowing.
- "Of this State" is a residue of scope `none`, because the run applies Nevada law.

**Reversal signals:**
- The parked-vehicle lamp provisions entering the corpus: compose them as `unless` on s4.
- A source showing that trailers are separated from their combinations.

## NRS_484D_215_1_o1 — multiple-beam use: reveal at a safe distance (surrogate)

**Decision.** The subject is a motor vehicle being operated (moving, or with its engine running) on
the roadway or shoulder. "During the times specified in NRS 484D.100" is a composition `as:
condition` on `NRS_484D_100_1`. That is the referred state itself: the composed rule's applicability
is exactly those times, for the same vehicle. "Subject to the following requirements and
limitations" composes `NRS_484D_215_1_o2` `as: exception`.

The obligation is a beam lit. Wherever the stopping distance exceeds the low beam's reveal distance,
the beam must be the high beam. The safe-distance standard is the whole content of this duty, so the
node is marked surrogate.

**Reason.** Beam aim and intensity are not observed. They are read through the beam state.

**Reversal signals:**
- Urban night recordings labelled compliant with low beams at moderate speed. That points either to
  `p.low_beam_reveal_distance` or to missing street-lighting evidence, which no atom carries.

## NRS_484D_215_1_o2 — dim for an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet

**Decision.** The trigger (motor vehicle being operated, roadway or shoulder, the times of 484D.100)
is shared with o1. The rule also needs a road user of the vehicle aggregate, other than the subject,
that is oncoming (`rel.oncoming`, headings opposed and closing). Its surface gap must be within the
literal 500 ft. The obligation is low beam.

The deeming sentence and its reference to DEF-NRS-484D-210-1-2 make the low beam compliant
regardless of road contour and loading. The validator allows one obligation span per node, so those
words are segmented as `definitional`. High beam is read as projecting glare; headlamps off do not
"use a distribution of light".

**Reversal signal:** a source that observes beam aim, or adaptive high beams that mask the oncoming
driver.

## Concept records

- **`drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry`** is a state, not an act. It counts from the
  observed entry onto the region (past operator `since`) until the body outline first stands at the
  clearance or more from it. The side of the region is not distinguished, and the contract says so.
- **`drv.motion.stopping_distance`** computes speed × reaction time plus speed² over twice the
  deceleration. Both inputs are formal parameters. It carries no adequacy bound: the calling rule
  compares the distance with its standard.

## For the operator

- **Gap on NRS-484D-100-1(c), "When directed by an official traffic control device".** No catalogue
  code of `dev.regulatory_sign` directs road users to display lamps. The proposal is a lamps-on sign
  (`dev.lamps_on_sign`, or equivalently a code `lamps_on` of `dev.regulatory_sign`). The validator
  only accepts a new id at the head of the proposal, which is why it is written that way. If the gap
  is filed, it blocks NRS_484D_100_1. Through their `as: condition` composition it also blocks both
  NRS_484D_215_1 nodes.
- **Parameter values proposed for review:**
  - `p.perception_reaction_time`: 2.5 s
  - `p.braking_decel_dry` / `p.braking_decel_wet` / `p.braking_decel_ice`: 4.5 / 3.4 / 1.5 m/s²
  - `p.curve_lateral_accel`: 3.0 m/s²
  - `p.lateral_margin_time`: 0.02 s
  - `p.traffic_time_headway`: 1.0 s
  - `p.low_beam_reveal_distance`: 30.48 m, from the 100 ft lowermost-beam figure of NRS 484D.210(2)
  - `p.oncoming_heading_cosine`: 0.7

  With the low-beam reach at 100 ft, the speed rule's o1 node requires high beams above roughly
  10 m/s at night. This is the strictest consequence of the surrogate, so review it first.
- **The definition of "stopping" against NRS-484B-560-7a.** DEF-NRS-484A-260's exception for
  traffic conflict would void clause (1) if applied literally. The plan does not apply it. Confirm
  this reading in the reading convention.

I've planned all five laws as six nodes, and the validator accepts every node and both new concepts. One law has a missing-vocabulary gap that will block it, and two other nodes depend on that law.

**Nodes**
- **`NRS_484B_560_7a`** (railroad crossing): once a vehicle has entered a level crossing, it must not halt until its trailing end is 15 ft past the crossing. A halt the police direct is excused. The causes the law gives ("insufficient space" or "undercarriage clearance") can't be observed, so any halt before the crossing is complete counts.
- **`NRS_484B_600_1a`** (basic speed rule): marked as a surrogate, meaning its verdicts are a policy reading rather than a legal conclusion. It sets one speed bound per factor the law names: stopping distance against sight distance and visibility (braking strength chosen by dry, wet or icy surface), speed on curves, room in the lane, and following time to the road user ahead.
- **`NRS_484B_769`** (cyclist and scooter signals): whenever the rider signals on a roadway, they must give an arm signal, and its meaning must match any lit indicator. The data records only what an arm signal means, not which arm gave it, so the manner of the signal can't be checked directly.
- **`NRS_484D_100_1`** (when lamps are required): headlamps must be lit at night, or when visibility is below 1,000 ft, or when a sign directs it. Parked vehicles are excused.
- **`NRS_484D_215_1_o1`** (beam choice, surrogate): headlamps must be lit, and high beam is required when stopping distance exceeds what the low beam reveals. It applies only at the times `NRS_484D_100_1` sets, and not when the next rule applies.
- **`NRS_484D_215_1_o2`** (dimming): with an oncoming vehicle within 500 ft, the low beam is required.

**New concepts**
- `drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry`: the road user has entered a region and is not yet a given distance clear of it.
- `drv.motion.stopping_distance`: how far a road user travels to a stop, given a reaction time and a braking rate.

**Needs your attention**
- **Gap:** clause (c) of `NRS_484D_100_1`, "when directed by an official traffic control device," has no sign in the vocabulary that orders lamps on. I proposed `dev.lamps_on_sign`; adding a `lamps_on` code to `dev.regulatory_sign` would do the same. The validator rejected the gap until the proposal began with a new atom id, which is why it's worded that way. If the gap is filed, it blocks that law and, through their dependency on it, both `NRS_484D_215_1` nodes.
- **Departure from a definition:** the definition of "stopping" excuses halts made to avoid conflict with other traffic. Applied literally, that would empty the railroad clause about insufficient space, so I didn't apply it. Please confirm this reading.
- **Strictest parameter value:** the low-beam reach is set to the 100 ft from NRS 484D.210. With it, `NRS_484D_215_1_o1` requires high beams at night above about 10 m/s, so it may flag ordinary urban driving on low beams. All proposed values are listed in `PLAN.md` for review.
